description:
OUTCOME LEDGER for the change-proportionality campaign this ticket anchored;
the live design work has moved to fz-kdt.74 (cells at name/arity). This
ticket stays open only as the epic-level acceptance: close when the
evals/distinct ratio on the three target fixtures drops materially below the
post-kdt.63 base (1,081/766/298-ish by the CLI lens; recipes matter -- CLI
vs PublicTrace differ, both valid).

## Landed by this campaign
- fz-kdt.63 (2acbc8d04): absence-is-not-retraction fold -- AnalyzeActivation
  evals 1,383 -> 1,081 (CLI lens, take_drop), retraction churn -> ~0. Its
  adversarial review discovered the widening-ladder/rebase coupling
  (fz-kdt.65) and the inventory moved both directions (pinned 59/221/214).
- fz-kdt.13.1 (6ef642f36): publisher identity = (Job, DerivationId) in the
  one ledger; behavior-neutral by five instruments incl. a 250-seed
  randomized differential.
- fz-kdt.62, .61, .56, .44 (see their tickets): the engine substrate.
- fz-kdt.69.1/.69.2: retraction sticks; three-valued callsite edges.

## Refuted by this campaign (kill reasons in fz-kdt.69 and .74's graveyard)
Cross-component settled-wait folding (ActivationInputs back-edge; main 79->64
not ->2-3, +31% blocked); finality-first pop (whole-body reads make the gate
invariant; provably dead); cause-scoped dirtiness (wrong set); live-edge
demand over value keys (edge is a strict subset of stated demand).

## The measured residual
Ascent height through sequential dataflow: main publishes ~55-57 REAL
content-changing evaluations; the multiplicative cascade breaks only by
dissolving the aggregation 2-cycle -- which is fz-kdt.74's stage-3 claim.
fz-kdt.13.2 is parked (see its ticket); fz-kdt.68's wait-attribution lever
remains valid if 74 stalls.

comments.text:
FOLDED FROM THREE TICKETS. fz-f98.5 ('telemetry-first convergence audit'), fz-f98.14 ('convergence runaway: drive is 1.3s') and fz-bfh.6 ('demand/analysis re-derivation volume, ~1.8k') were evaluated independently by three different agents, and all three arrived at the same measurement on the same fixture: 1382 AnalyzeActivation spans out of 2593 job spans on enum_take_drop_split.

They differed only in what they blamed, and each blame was stale in its own way: f98.5 blamed a schedule-dependent Seal<->DeriveRuntimeDemand<->Transport cycle (all those job kinds now grep to zero); f98.14 blamed SealSemanticClosure's monolithic reseal (deleted); bfh.6 paired AnalyzeActivation with DeriveRuntimeDemand re-derivation (runtime demand is now a pull product that settles 3 times per drive, not 1.8k).

Per [[feedback_fold_concordant_ideas]] they are one ticket. Keeping three would have had three people measure the same number and re-derive three dead diagnoses.

title: Change-proportional activation analysis: landed gains recorded; superseded by fz-kdt.74
